title: NonStationaryBrachistochrone: reproducibility package for controlled-rail brachistochrones in non-stationary spacetimes
description:
Symbolic derivations, numerical verification scripts, figure-generation code, laboratory design studies, and manuscript sources for controlled-rail brachistochrones in non-stationary spacetimes. The repository supports the companion studies of the FLRW and Vaidya sectors and of the conformal Kerr (Thakurta-Kerr) sector.

1.6.0 - bibliographic audit, experimental validation routes, and an independent review. Every source underpinning a claim in either manuscript was read at first hand rather than cited from memory or metadata. Forty-seven works were read at depth and thirty corrections followed, several of which changed what the papers assert.

What the audit found. Kovner's 1990 Fermat principle had been filed under the stationary case; his abstract covers nonstationary metrics and massive particles, the two adjectives this programme claims novelty for, so the distinction is now drawn explicitly on four grounds. What we had called the Fuglede-Ishihara dichotomy is Fuglede's definition of semiconformality, not a theorem, and the argument built on it was circular; Ishihara's own criterion then settles the question outright - the optical submersion is not a harmonic morphism, and the obstruction is the static-observer thrust. A Myers-type argument was a non sequitur, as Myers' own S^2 x S^2 example shows; retested on the Ricci tensor the hypothesis fails by sign, the optical scalar curvature being negative at every exterior point and every rail energy. Hamilton's four-manifold theorem had been applied to a three-dimensional base with compactness omitted. Three null-geodesic results had been cited as though they covered the timelike problem. Four results were credited to the wrong author, including Ree's shuffle, Ehrenfest's action-variable statement, and Dyer and Honig's conformal-Killing-horizon terminology.

What the audit gained. Giannoni and Piccione state in print, twice, that in the non-stationary case it is not even clear whether brachistochrones solve a second-order equation; the controlled rail is the other branch of their identity, which is the sharpest available statement of what is new here. The control-domain boundary turns out to have a 1997 precedent: Giannoni, Piccione and Verderesi restrict to |Y| < k, which is our compactness lemma. Sultana and Dyer supply a published necessary-and-sufficient criterion showing the Thakurta-Kerr conformal stationary limit surface is not a conformal Killing horizon, the twist being -a/2M on the equator and the test conformally invariant.

Experimental validation. Answered at three levels rather than declined. A bench - holonomic planar robot or XY stage - can emulate the reduced controlled system directly, reconstructing the indicatrix from 32 to 64 control directions and testing the first-order response and residual scaling. Analogue platforms already realise the geometry: rotational superradiance has been measured on a draining vortex and in superfluid helium, whose effective acoustic metric is a Randers structure with ergosurface at |v| = c, exactly the condition |W| = Ehat of the compactness lemma; expanding Bose-Einstein condensates supply the time-dependent scale factor. Gravitational validation is unavailable and is not claimed. A runnable design study for all three routes is under Experimental/, with the velocity oval built from the equatorial indicatrix rather than drawn generically - the identity closes to 4.4e-16.

An independent audit found three further defects, all corrected: Filippov's section III presupposes a convex velocity set, so it is no longer invoked for our boundary oval; the Fuglede correction had not been carried from Paper II to Paper I; and the out-of-plane Jacobi field lifts the conjugate-point statement to three dimensions but not global minimality, since the optical 3-manifold is simply connected while the equatorial surface has pi_1 = Z. The saturation step of the existence theorem is now a lemma with proof rather than an assertion.

Reproducibility. The provenance JSON carries a content digest over the reproducible content only, with wall-clock timings and the generation instant segregated in an environment block and excluded - they are the only quantities that legitimately differ between machines. Verified on a separate clone: identical digest, timings 13.0 s against 12.6 s. Twenty-two verification scripts, 203 checks, all passing.
